issue_context.title: Canceling `JSHost.ImportAsync` fails because `dynamic_import` in `invoke-js.ts` is not cancelable
comments:
Tagging subscribers to 'arch-wasm': @lewing See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description # TLDR: The cancellation token given to `JSHost.ImportAsync` does not work because the underlying JS function called by `ImportAsync` does not return a `Promise` that is "controllable" (outfitted with a special symbol). ```c# // Repro here: https://github.com/nikonthethird/ImportAsyncError, or paste this code into an InitializeAsync of a page in Blazor WASM: var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(); cts.Cancel(); await JSHost.ImportAsync("hello", "world.js", cts.Token); ``` The code above fails with an exception because [`dynamic_import`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ac3832812f9bc37fba2a66ac8987ca66d381d85/src/mono/wasm/runtime/invoke-js.ts#L177) is not controllable (the promise generated by the function is not wrapped using `wrap_as_cancelable_promise` like for example [`http_wasm_fetch`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ac3832812f9bc37fba2a66ac8987ca66d381d85/src/mono/wasm/runtime/http.ts#L52) is). # Description After upgrading to .NET 7, an application of mine has been throwing the following error messages in the log: ```text "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Rendering.WebAssemblyRenderer"]: Unhandled exception rendering component: "Error: Assert failed: Promise is not controllable" at System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript.CancelablePromise._CancelPromise(IntPtr ) at System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript.CancelablePromise.CancelPromise(Task ) at System.Net.Http.BrowserHttpInterop.<>c__DisplayClass13_0`1[[System.Int32, System.Private.CoreLib, Version=7.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e]].b__0() at System.Threading.CancellationToken.<>c.b__12_0(Object ) at System.Threading.CancellationTokenSource.Invoke(Delegate , Object , CancellationTokenSource ) at System.Threading.CancellationTokenSource.CallbackNode.<>c.b__9_0(Object ) at System.Threading.ExecutionContext.RunInternal(ExecutionContext , ContextCallback , Object ) --- End of stack trace from previous location --- ``` This is what I discovered: * [`JSHost.ImportAsync`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ac3832812f9bc37fba2a66ac8987ca66d381d85/src/libraries/System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript/src/System/Runtime/InteropServices/JavaScript/JSHostImplementation.cs#L272) calls `JavaScriptImports.DynamicImport`, then uses the `CancelationHelper` function to [call `CancelablePromise.CancelPromise`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ac3832812f9bc37fba2a66ac8987ca66d381d85/src/libraries/System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript/src/System/Runtime/InteropServices/JavaScript/JSHostImplementation.cs#L288) when the cancellation token fires. * [`CancelPromise`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ac3832812f9bc37fba2a66ac8987ca66d381d85/src/libraries/System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript/src/System/Runtime/InteropServices/JavaScript/CancelablePromise.cs#L14) calls [`mono_wasm_cancel_promise`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6251d496e307ed39f1e600cd036106cc1bd7e340/src/mono/wasm/runtime/cancelable-promise.ts#L26) which throws the error above [when the promise is not controllable](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6251d496e307ed39f1e600cd036106cc1bd7e340/src/mono/wasm/runtime/promise-controller.ts#L73), meaning when it does not have the promise control symbol. * However, the promise returned by [`JavaScriptImports.DynamicImport`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8aa77a952a285dcd318cf8e6c99ba6f99cec897f/src/libraries/System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript/src/System/Runtime/InteropServices/JavaScript/Interop/JavaScriptImports.Generated.cs#L46) is directly from [the async function `dynamic_import`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/fda0b358709e4b971b2cf546dff898f2ccaceb2c/src/mono/wasm/runtime/invoke-js.ts#L320), which is **NOT** wrapped with [`wrap_as_cancelable_promise`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/fda0b358709e4b971b2cf546dff898f2ccaceb2c/src/mono/wasm/runtime/cancelable-promise.ts#L19) like [all](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/fda0b358709e4b971b2cf546dff898f2ccaceb2c/src/mono/wasm/runtime/http.ts#L52) [the](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/fda0b358709e4b971b2cf546dff898f2ccaceb2c/src/mono/wasm/runtime/http.ts#L83) [others](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/fda0b358709e4b971b2cf546dff898f2ccaceb2c/src/mono/wasm/runtime/http.ts#L106) that use `CancelationHelper` are. Since .NET 7 uses the `[JSImport]` source generator internally, I suspect the exceptions I am experiencing also come from some internal `JSHost.ImportAsync` calls. ### Reproduction Steps ```razor @page "/" @using System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript

Hello, world!

@if (error is not null) {

@error

} @code { private String? error; protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync() { var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(); cts.Cancel(); try { await JSHost.ImportAsync("hello", "world.js", cts.Token); } catch (Exception ex) { error = ex.ToString(); } } } ``` A reproduction can [also be found here](https://github.com/nikonthethird/ImportAsyncError). ### Expected behavior The import should be cancelled. ### Actual behavior Error: Assert failed: Promise is not controllable ### Regression? Yes, no problem with my code in .NET 6. Note that I do not even use `JSHost.ImportAsync` in my code directly, but .NET 7 itself uses the new `[JSImport]` source generated, and this is where I expect the error to occur. ### Known Workarounds None so far. ### Configuration .NET 7.0.1 Ubuntu 20.04 / Firefox Windows 10 22H2 / Chromium x64 It happens in all cases, I don't know why I even provided this info... ### Other information _No response_

review_comments:
- Would it be useful add a short delay before the Cancel, to give a chance for `ImportAsync` get started?
- Also, would it be useful to have another test that tries to import from an external url?
- What about a test for importing a non-existent file - like `./non-existent.js`, and a url `https://www.foobar.com/non-existent.js`, and canceling for those?

The file is already in the browser cache so the promise would be fulfilled immediately and we would not see any cancelation at all.

I created ticket for it https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/80309

BTW the same infrastructure is used to cancel our WS on wasm. 
There are tests there which handle delayed cancelation/abort.
`src\libraries\System.Net.WebSockets.Client\tests\CancelTest.cs`
`src\libraries\System.Net.WebSockets.Client\tests\AbortTest.cs`
